title: Console MVP floorplan: minimal dashboards + graceful tracing & cost fallback
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Decision record and acceptance scope for a reduced-surface Console MVP focused on three high-value surfaces: a lightweight dashboards overview, resilient trace access with graceful degradation, and a compact cost-breakdown card. This ticket captures the cuts we make to hit launch commitment, the trade-offs, and operational acceptance criteria for QA and launch. The goal is to deliver immediate value for platform and product teams (route-level performance and cost signals) while deferring lower-priority details (custom dashboard builder, per-token heatmaps, long-term raw trace exploration) to subsequent phases.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Dashboard Overview shows per-route 95th latency, requests/sec (RPS), and error rate for the last 15 minutes and last 24 hours with date selector defaulted to 15m. Values must refresh within 60s of ingestion.

AC-2: Cost summary card displays daily aggregated cost for active routes (top 10 by traffic) and a 7-day trend sparkline. Cost calculation must use the Publishable cost model and match backend cost-accounting within 3% for test dataset.

AC-3: Trace access: Overview cards include a single-click link to the top correlated trace. If tracing backend responds, the trace viewer opens in a new tab with the sampled span timeline; if tracing backend is unavailable or rate-limited, the UI shows a clear non-blocking banner 'Tracing temporarily unavailable' and a link to raw request logs for the same timeframe.

AC-4: Performance SLOs for the Console pages: initial render of Dashboard Overview must be < 800ms at 90th percentile for typical user payloads (authentication + small dataset). Navigating to Cost card must be < 600ms at median.

AC-5: Rollout gating: feature flagging supports canary to 10% of orgs and an immediate kill switch. Canary telemetry (page loads, errors, fallback occurrences) must be collected to the staging telemetry pipeline before any customer canary is promoted.

AC-6: Error handling: Any backend failure (metrics, cost, tracing) must surface a distinct, actionable UI state and not break other cards. Example: metrics failure shows 'Metrics unavailable' card with a 'Retry' button and link to incident diagnostics.

AC-7: Security: access honors existing RBAC - users without observability role cannot see cost or traces and receive an informative permission error instead of a 500. This will be validated against a sample of 3 role permutations during QA.

AC-8: Documentation & runbook: A one-page runbook exists for on-call with steps for investigating dashboard/cost/tracing failures, and a short user-facing help doc is published in the Console help center with screenshots.

AC-9: Analytics: instrumented events for key UI states (dashboard_loaded, cost_card_failed, trace_fallback_shown) are emitted with minimal payload and appear in the telemetry workspace for verification.
AC-10: Backwards compatibility: public Redwood API keys and existing route identifiers continue to map to the same cost buckets; migrating customers to new cost model must be opt-in post-launch.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng (runtime + telemetry) and Design. Agreed to cut customizable dashboards and advanced cost breakdowns (per-token heatmap) for MVP.

2026-03-05: PM/Design alignment - UX will provide two small mockups: 'Overview (compact)' and 'Cost compact card'. Design link: https://confluence.redwood.company/console/mvp-floorplan (see mockups 1 & 2).
2026-03-08: Engineering estimated 5 story points; flagged dependency ENG-21421 (metrics ingest endpoint stabilization) and ENG-21900 (trace fetch proxy).
2026-03-10: Security review triage - RBAC check required; SSO edge cases deferred but must not block launch (security_review_required=false).
2026-03-12: Decision: tracing deep-dive and span search deferred to post-MVP. Implement trace link + fallback banner for launch to maintain reliability.

2026-03-14: Draft acceptance criteria posted. Requested QA plan and runbook from QA and Oncall leads. GitHub PRs for backend changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2304
acceptance_test_steps: Step 1: Deploy feature flag to staging and enable canary for internal org 'platform-alpha'
Step 2: Ingest synthetic traffic for 3 routes and verify Dashboard Overview metrics match synthetic generator within tolerance
Step 3: Simulate tracing backend outage and verify UI shows fallback banner and cost and metrics cards remain functional
Step 4: Run RBAC matrix test with 3 user roles to confirm permission gating
Step 5: Validate telemetry events appear in the telemetry workspace and that page performance SLOs are met
